claims.note: Product overview text for Mastercom Extended in the developer portal's machine-readable catalogue; the Mastercom support FAQ says the Extended API currently serves Single Message System disputes.

claims.claim: Mandate (2024): Mastercom API versions 2, 3, 4 and 5 were decommissioned in October 2024 and issuers and acquirers had to move to version 6 to keep processing disputes.
claims.quote: Mastercom decommissioned versions 2, 3, 4 and 5 of the Mastercom API in 2024. Issuers and acquirers must update their systems to version 6
claims.title: Release History (Mastercom)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Fetched as markdown. The Announcements page dates the decommissioning notice 'October 2024'.

claims.claim: Mandate (2025): Mastercom and Mastercom Extended API clients were required to switch from Entrust to DigiCert CA certificates before 24 March 2025 in production.
claims.quote: You are required to switch to DigiCert CA before March 24, 2025 in production
claims.title: Announcements (Mastercom Extended)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Fetched as markdown; dated 'February 2025'. Same notice appears on the Mastercom announcements page.

claims.claim: Mandate (2027): from 14 March 2027 in production Mastercard will automatically double the chargeback amount when credPostedAsPurchase=true, and issuers and acquirers coded to the current specification must change their integrations.
claims.quote: When `credPostedAsPurchase=true`, Mastercard automatically doubles the amount of the chargeback.
claims.title: Mastercom Announcements
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Dated 'September 2026'; MTF 05 March 2027, Production 14 March 2027; governed by GLB 14458.1 on the TRC.

claims.claim: Ethoca Consumer Clarity call-centre data is being integrated into Mastercom claims for Dual Message System issuers during 2026 (region-specific availability 13 July to 1 November 2026, excluding India, Indonesia, Nepal, Jordan and Tunisia).
claims.quote: provide Dual Message System issuers with enriched transaction data from Ethoca Consumer Clarity Call Center at the time of claim creation
claims.title: Mastercom Announcements
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Dated 'April 2026'; Release History gives availability 'July 13, 2026 to November 1, 2026' under GLB 12896.4.

claims.claim: Production access to the Mastercom API is gated on a signed Mastercard License Agreement (5-7 business day SLA), MTF validation by the Customer Implementation Service team, BIN/ARID entitlement in Access Manager within Mastercard Connect, and a 3-business-day key promotion SLA.
claims.quote: A user must have the correct Mastercom API BIN or ARID access in Access Manager within Mastercard Connect
claims.title: Onboarding Checklist (Mastercom)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Fetched as markdown. Sandbox is open on self-service sign-up; 'Service providers are provisioned by acquirers.'

claims.claim: Operational obligations for Mastercom integrators include rotating API keys, which expire every 13 months, and a throttling limit of 150 requests per second.
claims.quote: Mastercom API keys expire every 13 months, and expired keys can cause unexpected failures if they are not rotated in time.
claims.title: Support (Mastercom)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Fetched as markdown; FAQ also states 'all of our APIs are PCI compliant' and 'The throttling policy is as follows: 150 requests per second.'

claims.claim: Mandate (2024-2026): the First-Party Trust programme rejects No Cardholder Authorization chargebacks (reason code 5002 'First-Party Trust Reject') for U.S. domestic transactions effective 27 October 2024, expanding to Canada and Latin America/Caribbean from 21 January 2026 and to Asia Pacific (excluding Mainland China domestic, India and Nepal) from 19 April 2026.
claims.quote: Effective 27 October 2024: Both of the following occurred: The card was issued under a BIN or BIN range assigned to the United States.
claims.title: Chargeback Guide Merchant Edition (19 May 2026)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Retrieved from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine capture because mastercard.com/mastercard.us return HTTP 403 to non-browser clients; capture 2026-07-24; 'First-Party Trust' section, pages 564-565. Issuers can only re-chargeback with a notarised First-Party Trust Cardholder Exception Affidavit (Form 0830) or an attestation from the Chargeback contact in My Company Manager.

claims.claim: Trade press reported in March 2024 that Mastercard's First-Party Trust programme, first outlined in October 2023, would launch in the United States first during 2024, with Forter and Kount among early participants and participation optional for merchants.
claims.quote: Announced Monday, the Mastercard initiative is a new push for a program the network originally outlined in October.
claims.title: First-Party Fraud Continues to Bedevil Merchants, Mastercard Says
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Author Kevin Woodward. Predates the 27 October 2024 effective date shown in the Chargeback Guide.

claims.claim: In its FY2025 10-K Mastercard describes its 'franchise' as defining the technical, operational and financial standards all network participants must uphold, monitoring adherence, and operating a framework to resolve disputes between participants.
claims.quote: Operating Standards. We define the technical, operational and financial standards that all network participants are required to uphold
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Filing accession 0001141391-26-000013. Same passage: 'Issue Resolution. We operate a framework to address disputes between our network participants'. Text was read from a copy downloaded to the shared scratchpad; SEC.gov blocked this session's direct requests as an undeclared automated tool.

claims.claim: The 10-K's risk factors state Mastercard routinely encounters account data compromise events at merchants and third-party processors, the operational reality behind its ADC rules.
claims.quote: we also routinely encounter account data compromise events involving merchants and third-party payment processors that process, store or transmit payment transaction data
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Item 1A Risk Factors.

claims.claim: Mastercard Connect, the portal on which Mastercom, the Technical Resource Center, My Company Manager, Variance Manager and other rule-related tools live, presents only a sign-in page to the public.
claims.quote: Mastercard Connect
claims.title: Mastercard Connect (sign-in)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Root URL 302-redirects to /-/sign-in?referral_path=%2F; the only visible text is the page title. trc-techresource.mastercard.com serves a JavaScript shell reading 'Loading application...'.

claims.claim: Mastercard Engage, the partner programme referenced from the rules page navigation, is login-gated on the developer portal and returns an authorisation error to unauthenticated requests.
claims.quote: Session expired.
claims.title: Mastercard Engage (login redirect)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: HTTP 401 with JSON {"code":"DP10005","message":"Session expired."} after redirect to /devzone/api/user/login?...referral_path=%2Fengage%2F.

claims.claim: Rules training is routed to Mastercard Academy, which the rules page links as the venue for training sessions; the Academy site itself is a JavaScript-only application unreadable to non-browser clients.
claims.quote: Explore training sessions via the Mastercard Academy.
claims.title: Mastercard Rules for Merchants - Customer Compliance Program
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Retrieved from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine capture because mastercard.com/mastercard.us return HTTP 403 to non-browser clients; capture 2026-01-03. academy.mastercard.com returned 'You need to enable javascript to view this website.'

claims.claim: Mastercard's Dispute Resolution Management (DRM) team offers training for issuers, acquirers and processors on the chargeback and compliance processes.
claims.quote: The Dispute Resolution Management (DRM) team offers convenient, flexible training options for issuers, acquirers, and processors.
claims.title: Chargebacks Made Simple Guide
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Retrieved from the Internet Archive Wayback Machine capture because mastercard.com/mastercard.us return HTTP 403 to non-browser clients; capture 2026-09-20; section 1.3.

claims.claim: A processor's public release guide states that most network operating-rule changes, Mastercard's included, arrive in two release periods a year, Spring and Fall, and republishes each Mastercard item with its effective date.
claims.quote: Most of the changes come during two release periods – Spring and Fall.
claims.title: April 2026 Release Guide (Spring 2026 Updates)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Page states 'The information in this document is accurate as of March 2026'. Its Mastercard table lists: Not Reversed or Cleared Preauthorization TPE criteria 4/1/26; Digital Enablement Fee US 4/6/26; Specialty Merchant Registration Program fees (varies); TPE pricing EU 10/1/26; Authorization Acquirer Exemption Indicator Fee EU 10/12/26.

claims.claim: Mandate (1 April 2026): under revised Not Reversed or Cleared Preauthorization TPE criteria, acquirers must submit a full reversal within 30 days of the original authorization for any preauthorization that is never cleared.
claims.quote: for preauthorizations where no clearing message is submitted, acquirers must ensure a full reversal is submitted within 30 days from original auth date
claims.title: April 2026 Release Guide (Spring 2026 Updates)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Regions AP/CAN/LAC/MEA/US. Same page: 'any preauthorization request that is subsequently followed by one or more incremental preauthorization will be excluded from the Not Reversed or Cleared Preauthorization TPE program.'

claims.claim: An issuer processor (SoFi Tech Solutions, formerly Galileo) states that networks communicate mandates through technical newsletters four times a year, and it republishes every Mastercard bulletin it must support by GLB number with effective date.
claims.quote: Card networks communicate these mandates through technical newsletters four times a year.
claims.title: Card Network Mandates - Introduction
claims.publisher: SoFi Tech Solutions (formerly Galileo Financial Technologies)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: docs.galileo-ft.com/pro/docs/card-network-mandates now 301-redirects here. Page groups Mastercard bulletins by year and half (H1/H2) with 'Impact to SoFi Tech Solutions' for each, e.g. GLB 8701.1, GLB 11738.1, GLB 12516.1, GLB 13264.2, CAN/EUR/MEA/US 13437.2.

claims.claim: Mandate (17 October 2025): Mastercard bulletin GLB 8701.1 introduced Transaction Link Identifier (TLID) subelements and subfields for lifecycle linking; a later revision, GLB 8701.3, extends TLID effective 2 June 2026.
claims.quote: Effective 17 Oct 2025, Mastercard introduced subelements and subfields to support multiuse transaction identification data
claims.title: Card Network Mandates - Introduction
claims.publisher: SoFi Tech Solutions (formerly Galileo Financial Technologies)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Same page: 'GLB 8701.3 — Enhancing Mastercard Transaction Link Identifier Effective June 2, 2026'. The TLID field 'contains DE105SF1'. Corroborated by MAG Insights (2025-04-15): 'Starting October 17, 2025, this TLID needs to stick with the transaction all the way through its lifecycle.'

claims.claim: Mandate (2 June 2026): GLB 11738.1 introduced near-real-time age verification, requiring acquirers to carry merchant age-threshold requests and issuers to return results.
claims.quote: GLB 11738.1 — Introducing age verification capability Effective June 2, 2026, Mastercard is introducing near real-time age verification
claims.title: Card Network Mandates - Introduction
claims.publisher: SoFi Tech Solutions (formerly Galileo Financial Technologies)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Rivero AG (2026-08-13) describes the same change as part of 'Mastercard's 2nd June network processing release' and says 'Mastercard mandates testing for this release'.

claims.claim: Mandate (2 June 2026): GLB 12516.1 has Mastercard populate a Transaction Type Identifier on the acquirer's behalf for transactions from merchants registered in the Specialty Merchant Registration Program, exposing high-risk registration status to issuers.
claims.quote: Effective June 2, 2026, Mastercard is populating a new Transaction Type Identifier (TTI) value on behalf of an acquirer in authorization request and clearing messages
claims.title: Card Network Mandates - Introduction
claims.publisher: SoFi Tech Solutions (formerly Galileo Financial Technologies)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Same page: the identifier 'signifies that the acquirer and, if applicable, the payment facilitator sponsoring the specialty merchant are held to high standards and controls'.

claims.claim: Mandate (23 October 2026): bulletin CAN/EUR/MEA/US 13437.2 introduces a card-level Spend Auth Score (001-100) in authorization; issuers are only required to be able to receive it.
claims.quote: The mandate requires only that issuers be able to receive the score
claims.title: Card Network Mandates - Introduction
claims.publisher: SoFi Tech Solutions (formerly Galileo Financial Technologies)
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Same page lists other 23 October 2026 items: GLB 13261.2 (AAV leading indicators kD/kV), GLB 13264.2 (P2P TTIs C09/F09), GLB 13386.2 (MDES digital payment data).

claims.claim: Mastercard network releases are named by year and quarter and land in April and October: an issuer processor reports certification against Release 26.Q2 (effective 17 April 2026) and Release 26.Q4 (effective 23 October 2026).
claims.quote: The Marqeta platform is certified with the April 2026 Mastercard Release 26.Q2, effective 17 April 2026.
claims.title: Card Network Certifications 2026
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Same page: 'Marqeta is certified with the October 2026 Mastercard Release 26.Q4, effective 23 October 2026.' Visa's parallel April 2026 VisaNet Business Enhancements are also dated 17 April 2026.

claims.claim: Mandate (17 April 2026): GLB 12192.1 adds Transaction Type Identifier P76 for fiat-backed stablecoins and CBDCs alongside P70 for floating cryptocurrencies, so processors must distinguish crypto purchase types.
claims.quote: Effective 17 April 2026, Mastercard is enhancing indicators to distinguish between different types of cryptocurrency used for purchases.
claims.title: Card Network Certifications 2026
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Marqeta maps P76 'to the existing CRYPTOCURRENCY_PURCHASE special condition indicator'. Mastercard bulletin AP/LAC/MEA/US 12568.1 uses the same TTIs (P70/P76 crypto, P71 high-risk securities, P72 other specialty) to bill Specialty Merchant fees.

claims.claim: Rules changes ship as a numbered Global Operations Bulletin paired with a 'System Release' technical annex (e.g. the 26.Q2 Combined Dual and Single Message Annex) that issuers and acquirers must test against.
claims.quote: refer to Mastercard Global Operations Bulletin 11738.1 and the System Release 26.Q2 Combined Dual and Single Message Annex
claims.title: Mastercard's age verification mandate: What card issuers and acquirers must do
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: No individual byline (Rivero AG, Zurich, a scheme-compliance vendor). Also: 'the QA team must utilise the System Release 26.Q2 v1 Combined Dual and Single Message Annex.'

claims.claim: Mandate (17 June 2025): Mastercard stopped accepting 'undefined' authorizations; every authorization must be flagged as a preauthorization or a final authorization, with a renamed processing-integrity fee applied to approved undefined authorizations from 1 July 2025.
claims.quote: you'll no longer be able to submit transactions without clearly identifying them as either a pre-authorization or a final authorization
claims.title: Everything You Need to Know: Brand Release Updates
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Authors Joe Vasterling and Monica Gullickson (Best Buy). Same article: 'Then, on July 1, 2025, Mastercard will: Rename and update the PIF Fee ... Increase this fee every January for the next two years.' Opens with 'like clockwork—updates from the payment card networks' tied to April 11, 2025 effective dates.

claims.claim: Mastercard bulletin AP/LAC/MEA/US 12568.1 (published 28 October 2025) restructures Specialty Merchant Registration Program pricing with staggered effective dates of 1 May 2026, 3 June 2026 and first billing 14 June 2026.
claims.quote: Published: 28 October 2025 Effective: 1 May 2026 3 June 2026 14 June 2026
claims.title: AP/LAC/MEA/US 12568.1 New and Updated Specialty Merchant Registration Program Fees for the United States, Middle East/Africa Regions, and Select Countries in the Asia/Pacific and Latin America and the Caribbean Regions
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Third-party-hosted copy of a Mastercard Connect bulletin (PDF metadata title matches; '© 2025 Mastercard. Proprietary.'); authenticity cannot be checked against the portal. Header: Type Bulletin announcement; Category Pricing/Fees; Audience Acquirer, Processor; Action indicator Financial. Billing table: Specialty Merchant Registration Program SC USD 1,000 annual per merchant registration; Specialty Merchant Transaction Fee 0.02; Braintree's release guide lists the same fees with CA 6/1/26, EU 10/1/26, JP 1/1/29.

claims.claim: Acquiring for specialty (high-risk) merchants requires a Mastercard supplemental licence: new acquirers must file the High-Risk License Addendum (Form 637) and be approved, and a USD 50,000 annual High-Risk Acquirer License Fee applies from 1 May 2026.
claims.quote: New acquirers that would like to acquire and register specialty merchants must submit the High-Risk License Addendum (Form 637) and be approved by Mastercard
claims.title: AP/LAC/MEA/US 12568.1 New and Updated Specialty Merchant Registration Program Fees for the United States, Middle East/Africa Regions, and Select Countries in the Asia/Pacific and Latin America and the Caribbean Regions
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Billing table row: 'High-Risk Acquirer License Fee MA 50,000 Annual' (billing event 2MA1002). Existing specialty acquirers are granted the supplemental licence automatically but still billed; acquirers that opt out 'must unregister and terminate their relationships with all specialty merchants'.

claims.claim: Mastercard announcements carry a structured header (Type, Category, Audience, Region, Brand, Action Indicator, Published, Effective) plus a version history, with 'Brand mandate' as an action indicator; AN 6977 (11 October 2022) is a publicly mirrored example.
claims.quote: Type: Bulletin announcement Category: Operations Rules/Standards Audience: Acquirer Merchant Processor Network enablement partner Region: Global Brand: Mastercard® Action Indicator: Brand mandate
claims.title: AN 6977 Revised Standards for Merchants Utilizing a Subscription/Recurring Payments Model or Negative Option Billing Model
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Predates the 24-month window; included for announcement format. Third-party-hosted copy; authenticity not checkable against Mastercard Connect. Body ties programme identification to sanctions: a merchant flagged four-plus months in the ACMP that has not implemented the receipt requirement 'may be subject to Category A noncompliance assessments each month, which will be in addition to the assessments applicable under the ACMP'.

claims.claim: Mandate (1 April 2027): per practitioner reporting of bulletin GLB 14127.1 (published 28 July 2026 on Mastercard Connect), the Acquirer Chargeback Monitoring Program is replaced by a Global Merchant Audit Program that scores acquirers as well as merchants on a combined fraud-plus-chargeback ratio.
claims.quote: Mastercard is retiring the Acquirer Chargeback Monitoring Program and replacing it with a single framework: the Global Merchant Audit Program, or GMAP.
claims.title: Mastercard GMAP Explained: What Acquirers Need to Know Before April 2027
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: No byline or dateline; text references the 28 July 2026 bulletin. Bulletin title quoted as 'Revised Standards for the Acquirer Chargeback Monitoring Program (ACMP), the Global Merchant Audit Program (GMAP), and the Questionable Merchant Audit Program (QMAP)'. New categories: High Dispute Merchant (HDM), Excessive Dispute Merchant (EDM), High Dispute Acquirer (HDA), Excessive Dispute Acquirer (EDA); ratio '(FLD fraud reports + non-fraud chargebacks) ÷ prior month's sales'. Site's own sourcing note says figures are 'corroborated across multiple independent payments-compliance sources' and the bulletin 'is not publicly posted'.

claims.claim: Practitioner source confirms Mastercard's rule-change bulletins are distributed only to member institutions through Mastercard Connect and are not published on the open web, which is why programme changes such as GMAP have no public press release.
claims.quote: network bulletins go straight to the member institutions they govern, not the open web
claims.title: Mastercard GMAP Explained: What Acquirers Need to Know Before April 2027
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Consistent with Mastercard's own Chargebacks Made Simple Guide, which locates Announcements in the Technical Resource Center on Mastercard Connect.

claims.claim: Mandate (1 April 2027): EFM, ECM and HECM monitoring moves from the merchant ID to the sub-merchant ID wherever one is populated, removing payment facilitators' ability to dilute one sub-merchant inside an aggregate MID.
claims.quote: starting April 1, 2027, EFM, ECM, and HECM monitoring shifts from the Merchant ID (MID) to the sub-merchant ID wherever one is populated
claims.title: Mastercard GMAP Explained: What Acquirers Need to Know Before April 2027
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Same source: ECM ratio thresholds 'hold steady through 2028, then step down each January from 2029 through 2031'.

claims.claim: Mandate (enforcement 23 October 2026; assessments from 31 January 2027): under GLB 12940.1 merchants must pass the retained TLID on subsequent merchant-initiated transactions, with reported non-compliance assessments of USD 2,500-5,000 per month capped at USD 25,000 under the Data Integrity Monitoring Program.
claims.quote: reportedly ranging from $2,500 to $5,000 per month, capped at $25,000 and assessed under the Data Integrity Monitoring Program (DIMP)
claims.title: Mastercard TLID and Subscriptions: Are you ready?
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Author Melissa Shields, Head of Payments Strategy. Timeline on page: 17 Oct 2025 issuers/processors pass TLID (lifecycle); Dec 2025 GLB 8701 update; Jan 2026 GLB 12940.1 released with CIT-MIT 'Economic Linking'; 2 June 2026 merchants/acquirers must retain TLID from initial CITs; 23 Oct 2026 'Enforcement begins'. Amounts are flagged 'reportedly' by the author.

claims.claim: Mandate (4 January 2027): Mastercard will decommission Acquirer Collaboration in the US and Canada under bulletin CAN/US 14059.1, closing new enrolment on 21 July 2026 when the bulletin published, without naming a replacement platform.
claims.quote: Mastercard will decommission Acquirer Collaboration in the US and Canada on January 4, 2027, per bulletin CAN/US 14059.1.
claims.title: Mastercard Acquirer Collaboration Ends in January 2027
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Page HTML served only a JavaScript shell to curl; quote is as returned by WebFetch and matched the search-engine snippet. Also per WebFetch: 'New enrollment closed on July 21, 2026, the day the bulletin published' and 'direct Ethoca registration is the available path today'. Compare Chargeback Gurus (2022) reporting acquirers were added to Mastercom Collaboration in July 2022.

claims.claim: Mandate (1 January 2026): revised standards for Mastercard's Merchant Monitoring Program (MMP) took effect, per a merchant-monitoring vendor that pairs it with Visa's VAMP enforcement date of 1 October 2025.
claims.quote: Mastercard’s Merchant Monitoring Program (MMP) revised standards take effect
claims.title: Why the Next 6 Months Will Redefine Merchant Risk Management
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Byline 'by LegitScript Folks' (no named author); vendor page. Full sentence: 'Just three months later, on January 1, 2026, Mastercard's Merchant Monitoring Program (MMP) revised standards take effect.' MMP is not named in the public Security Rules Merchant Edition.

contradictions.a: Mastercard Rules 3 June 2025 (page 169) requires registration in the 'Mastercard Registration Program (MRP) system using Mastercard Connect'
contradictions.b: Mastercard Rules 2 June 2026 contains no '(MRP) system' wording and its summary of changes cites 'GLB 12564 Revised Standards for the Specialty Merchant Registration Program' (7.8.3)

contradictions.a: Security Rules and Procedures 11 February 2025 (8.3.2) says ECP merchants are monitored 'through the Data Integrity Online application on Mastercard Connect'
contradictions.b: Security Rules and Procedures 4 August 2026 (8.3.2) says 'through the Data Integrity application on Mastercard Connect'

contradictions.a: A Wayback capture of the legacy mastercard.us Mastercard Rules URL dated 2026-01-15 serves the 3 June 2025 edition (484 pages)
contradictions.b: The mastercard.com rules-pdfs path served the 2 June 2026 edition (503 pages) by 2026-09-20, so the same document title carried two edition dates and page counts depending on URL

contradictions.a: Chargeback Gurus (2025-10-21) states ECM = 100+ chargebacks and >1.5% for two consecutive months, HECM = 300+ and 3%, with a fine table from USD 1,000 to 200,000
contradictions.b: Mastercard's public Security Rules (4 August 2026, 8.3) give no thresholds or amounts, deferring to 'Edit 2' of the gated Data Integrity Monitoring Program manual

contradictions.a: Mastercard Rules 3 June 2025 metadata labels the document 'Type Brand-related standards'
contradictions.b: Mastercard Rules 2 June 2026 metadata labels it 'Type Product or Service Guide: Legal and compliance standards'

contradictions.a: SoFi Tech Solutions lists the issuer-initiated P2P transaction-type bulletin as 'GLB 13264.2 — Issuer-Initiated Person-to-Person (P2P) Transactions', effective October 23, 2026
contradictions.b: Marqeta lists the same change as 'GLB 13264.1 - Identifying issuer-initiated person-to-person payment and funding transactions', effective 23 October 2026 (different revision suffix)

contradictions.a: Marqeta states the 'April 2026 Mastercard Release 26.Q2' is effective 17 April 2026
contradictions.b: Rivero AG attributes age verification (GLB 11738.1, effective 2 June 2026 per SoFi) to 'Mastercard's 2nd June network processing release' while citing the 'System Release 26.Q2' annex, so the same release label is tied to two effective dates

contradictions.a: Chargeback Gurus (2025-10-21) presents ECP thresholds as stable (ECM 100+/1.5%, HECM 300+/3%)
contradictions.b: SLYCE360 reports that under GLB 14127.1 the ECM ratio thresholds 'hold steady through 2028, then step down each January from 2029 through 2031' and monitoring moves to sub-merchant ID from 1 April 2027
